title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 4 Jul to 26 Sep 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 26 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.86 km2 to 29.82 km2, or -6.4%, over 84 days. The land changed little in HV, while HH rose slightly.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 2.04 km2. Mean HV moved by -0.06 dB and mean HH rose by 0.4 dB. In HH, 2.51 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 0.27 km2 darker; in HV, 0.72 km2 turned brighter and 0.38 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 1.0 km2 brighter in HH. The open water type had 0.61 km2 brighter in HH and rose 0.47 dB. The changing fields type rose 1.06 dB in HH, and built-up land rose 0.49 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's records would confirm it. Possible cause for the brighter shore: ground left dry by falling water echoes more than water does. Possible cause for higher HH on built-up land: a small calibration difference between the dates; stable targets on more dates would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 12.7% and 9.2% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use this pair, with no flag on either date, for a summer drawdown figure, and check it against the dam's records. Map the shore segments that brightened in HH.
